work.what: In lean/Erdos359.lean (namespace ZetaLean.Erdos359, statement-only lean_lib outside the certified arm; a `sorry` is permitted there and banned in lean/ZetaLean/*.lean), define the greedy sequence of Erdos problem 359 and connect it to the already-stated Porubsky hypothesis. Erdos problem 359 reads: 'Let a_1 < a_2 < ... be an infinite sequence of integers such that a_1 = n and a_{i+1} is the least integer which is not a sum of consecutive earlier a_j s. What can be said about the density of this sequence? In particular, in the case n = 1, can one prove that a_k / k -> infinity and a_k / k^{1+c} -> 0 for any c > 0?' For n = 1 the sequence begins 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 14, 15. The conjectured asymptotic is a_k ~ k log k / log log k. Two deliverables: (a) a Lean definition `greedy : Nat -> Nat -> Nat` with `greedy n 0 = n` and `greedy n (j+1)` the least natural number that is not a sum of consecutive terms among `greedy n 0, ..., greedy n j`; (b) a proof (not a sorry) that `greedy 1` satisfies `ZetaLean.Erdos359.IsConsecutiveSumComplete`, which is defined in that file as `def IsConsecutiveSumComplete (g : Nat -> Nat) : Prop := forall n : Nat, 0 < n -> exists a b : Nat, a <= b /\ (sum over i in Finset.Icc a b of g i) = n`. The reason (b) holds: an integer that is not a sum of consecutive earlier terms is by construction enrolled as the next term, and a single term is a sum of one consecutive term. That is what makes Porubsky's lemma applicable to problem 359 at all. Also prove `StrictMono (greedy 1)`. A `decide`-level check that the first eight terms of `greedy 1` are 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 14, 15 is a cheap correctness guard on the definition and is worth including.

Prove `ZetaLean.Erdos359.porubsky_liminf_eq_zero` in lean/Erdos359.lean, replacing its single `sorry`. The statement as it stands, verbatim: `theorem porubsky_liminf_eq_zero (g : Nat -> Nat) (hmono : StrictMono g) (hcomplete : IsConsecutiveSumComplete g) (eps : Real) (heps : 0 < eps) : Filter.liminf (fun k : Nat => (g k : Real) * Real.log (Real.log (k : Real)) / ((k : Real) * Real.log (k : Real) ^ (1 + eps))) Filter.atTop = 0`, where `IsConsecutiveSumComplete g` means `forall n : Nat, 0 < n -> exists a b : Nat, a <= b /\ (sum over i in Finset.Icc a b of g i) = n` and the exponent `(1 + eps)` is real so the power is `Real.rpow`. This is Porubsky's 1977 result (Nieuw Archief voor Wiskunde), cited on erdosproblems.com problem 359 via Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory (1981). The published statement is: for every strictly increasing sequence a_k such that every positive integer can be written as a sum of one or more consecutive elements, and every eps > 0, liminf (a_k log log k) / (k (log k)^{1+eps}) = 0. Porubsky's paper also gives the equivalent-looking form 'for any eps > 0 there are infinitely many k with a_k < (log k)^eps * k log k / log log k', and the companion result 'if A(x) counts the a_i <= x then limsup A(x)/pi(x) >= 1/log 2'. The counting form is likely the easier route to the liminf form. Do NOT weaken the statement to get it through: if the proof needs a lemma Mathlib lacks, report that lemma as new work instead. Note this repo's Lean has no existing `liminf`/`limsup` usage to copy idioms from; `Filter.atTop` idioms live in lean/ZetaLean/HardyRamanujantheorem.lean. Mathlib is pinned at v4.33.0-rc2. The literature source (Porubsky 1977) could not be fetched during the statement attempt: www.erdosproblems.com returns HTTP 403 to automated requests, so the argument will have to be reconstructed or the paper obtained by other means.

State Erdos problem 359 itself in Lean, alongside Porubsky's lemma in lean/Erdos359.lean (namespace ZetaLean.Erdos359). The problem: 'Let a_1 < a_2 < ... be an infinite sequence of integers such that a_1 = n and a_{i+1} is the least integer which is not a sum of consecutive earlier a_j s. What can be said about the density of this sequence? In particular, in the case n = 1, can one prove that a_k / k -> infinity and a_k / k^{1+c} -> 0 for any c > 0?' Three statements to write, each over the greedy sequence for n = 1: (I) `Filter.Tendsto (fun k => (a k : Real) / (k : Real)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop`; (II) for every `c : Real` with `0 < c`, `Filter.Tendsto (fun k => (a k : Real) / (k : Real) ^ (1 + c)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)`; (III) the conjectured asymptotic `a_k ~ k log k / log log k`, i.e. `Filter.Tendsto (fun k => (a k : Real) * Real.log (Real.log (k : Real)) / ((k : Real) * Real.log (k : Real))) Filter.atTop (nhds 1)`. All three are open, so all three are `sorry` and must stay outside lean/ZetaLean/*.lean, which CI holds to zero sorrys. Depends on the greedy sequence definition existing first. For cross-checking the formalization, Google DeepMind's formal-conjectures repository has FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/359.lean with the same four claims (I, II, the first-eight-terms computation, and the asymptotic), all sorried, under Apache-2.0; do not copy its text into this MIT repo, but it is a valid reference for whether a statement is faithful.
